advisory.checklist_item: - [ ] Strengthen the assert_env_ready url assertions so they distinguish 'url flagged as missing' from the always-present 'base_url' hint text (e.g. assert the message begins with the 'missing ... configuration:' clause and that 'url' appears there, not merely anywhere).
evidence: assert_env_ready message: `"(set url via [tool.rebar.reconciler].base_url; JIRA_PAT is env-only) "` (backend.py:270) always contains the substring 'url'

test_assert_env_ready_names_each_missing_essential parametrizes `({"url": ""}, "url")` then asserts `expected_token.lower() in str(exc.value).lower()` (line 143) — tautologically true regardless of whether url was flagged
test_assert_env_ready_reports_every_missing_essential_at_once asserts `"url" in message and "jira_pat" in message` (line 153); the 'jira_pat' half is sound, the 'url' half is not
advisory.finding: The assert_env_ready tests assert `"url" in message` to verify a missing url is named, but the fixed error-message text always contains the substring 'url' (via '...base_url...'). So these assertions pass even if the code failed to flag a missing url — they do not actually verify the url essential was collected into the `missing` list.
advisory.suggested_fix: Assert against the leading 'missing Jira Data Center configuration: <names>' clause specifically — e.g. split on ':' and check the token list before the parenthetical hints — so the always-present 'base_url' hint cannot satisfy the check.

advisory.checklist_item: - [ ] Assert a populated `RemoteRef.instance` (and, per the docstring, a `jira-` local-id prefix) on the DC-created ticket in test_a_dc_created_ticket_carries_the_shared_jira_provenance, not just `creation_channel`.
evidence: Test body asserts only: `assert ticket.get("creation_channel") == "jira"` (test_reconcile_pass.py:295)
Docstring claims more than is asserted: "with the DEPLOYMENT distinguished by ``RemoteRef.instance``" (test_reconcile_pass.py:253) and "a ``jira-`` local-id prefix" (module docstring line 13)
AC (rebar:b4e3-1de0-3188-40a1): "a DC-created ticket is asserted ... to carry `creation_channel == "jira"` and a populated `RemoteRef.instance`"
grep of tests/external/live_jira_dc shows `instance` occurs only in docstrings/error strings (lines 15, 253, 297), never in an assertion — the populated-instance contract is untested
advisory.finding: The live provenance test asserts only `creation_channel == "jira"` but never asserts a populated `RemoteRef.instance`, which the ticket AC explicitly requires ("a DC-created ticket is asserted ... to carry `creation_channel == "jira"` and a populated `RemoteRef.instance`") and which the test's own docstring claims to pin. A regression that leaves the deployment-distinguishing `instance` empty — the exact failure the epic's shared-identity decision guards against — passes undetected.
scenarios: A DC deployment fails to stamp RemoteRef.instance (or stamps a shared/empty value), collapsing the per-deployment identity the epic depends on — the test still passes.
advisory.suggested_fix: After the creation_channel assertion, extract the RemoteRef (or its serialized instance field) from `ticket` and assert it is non-empty and names the DC deployment, e.g. `assert ticket-derived instance, ...` — mirroring the AC's "populated RemoteRef.instance".

advisory.checklist_item: - [ ] Make the idempotence test seed a real local ticket (or a remote issue), assert the FIRST pass actually applies a mutation, then assert the SECOND pass writes nothing — so convergence, not an empty-store no-op, is verified.
evidence: `dc_rebar_repo` only writes config; it builds on `rebar_repo`, which runs `rebar.init_repo(...)` and creates NO tickets (tests/external/conftest.py:167)

Test asserts nothing about the FIRST pass writing: `first = _run_reconcile(...); _assert_no_unhandled_exception(first, ...)` then only checks the SECOND pass `mutations_applied == 0` (test_reconcile_pass.py:226-235)

Docstring/Testing intent is convergence-after-write: "A second pass immediately after the first must be a no-op" (line 224); ticket Testing: "a full reconcile pass ... creates a remote issue from a local ticket ... and a second pass is a no-op"
With an empty local store the first pass has nothing to push, so the no-op assertion holds without ever exercising the write-then-converge path
advisory.finding: The idempotence test seeds no local ticket and asserts no first-pass write, so both bootstrap-strict passes can legitimately apply zero mutations against the empty store; `mutations_applied == 0` on the second pass is then vacuously true and does not demonstrate convergence (its stated purpose). A backend whose push is broken and always writes nothing would pass this test.
scenarios: A regression where DC outbound push silently no-ops (or fails to record applied mutations) still yields mutations_applied==0 on both passes — the idempotence test stays green.
advisory.suggested_fix: Create a local ticket in dc_rebar_repo before the first pass (or reuse the provenance test's remote-issue seed), assert `first`'s envelope reports mutations_applied > 0, then assert `second`'s mutations_applied == 0.
